subject: Private offer & partner uplift: structuring Acme deal on AWS Marketplace
messages:
From: Amy Jensen <amy.jensen@acme.io>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: partners@cloudresell.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in a private offer + distributor commission (Acme)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Acme is keen to proceed but we'd like to buy via our preferred reseller (CloudResell) through AWS Marketplace private offer. They asked whether Redwood can: (1) apply a customer-level discount off list for a privately negotiated price, and (2) provide a reseller commission / uplift for CloudResell to get their margin.

High-level asks from procurement: 10–15% off list for the end customer; reseller needs a minimum 15% uplift (they want to earn their margin & cover implementation). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports the following on AWS Marketplace: private offers with two-sided pricing (customer discount + partner uplift), and any constraints around SKU bundling?

We'd also like an indicative pricing/commission structure so internal execs can greenlight. Timeline is tight — target start of September.

Thanks,
Amy Jensen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Technologies

[Attachment: procurement_terms.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in a private offer + distributor commission (Acme)

Amy — appreciate the note and the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can structure this as a private offer on AWS Marketplace with an end-customer price and an allocated reseller commission. There are a few implementation choices that affect accounting and unit economics — see below.

Options (quick):
- Option A (Marketplace discount): Apply a customer-level discount on the AWS private offer price; Redwood invoices the customer at the discounted list via the marketplace flow. Reseller gets a separate commission off Redwood's gross.
- Option B (Bundled reseller SKU): Create a partner-bundled SKU (Reseller markup included) on Marketplace; reseller uplift baked into price, simpler for payout but less transparent for customer-level discounting.

Initial proposal to get the deal moving: Redwood list price -> allow a 12% customer discount (applied as AWS private offer) + reseller commission of 18% rev-share to CloudResell (paid monthly). That combination keeps our gross margin above our internal threshold for deals of this size.

I'm attaching a simple model showing unit economics for these levers. Can finance confirm the acceptable commission cap?

[Attachment: margin_model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in a private offer + distributor commission (Acme)

Priyom / Karthik — ran the numbers against our 2026 revenue model and the proposed 18% reseller commission + 12% customer discount is tight but workable for a 12–18 month committed ARR if ACV > $250k. Two notes:

- Recommend capping partner uplift at 18% (vs 20%) for AWS private offers that include customer discounts — beyond 18% the gross margin to Redwood drops below our floor for strategic accounts.
- If we structure as a bundled reseller SKU, margin leakage is higher because we lose transparency on token/unit economics; prefer marketplace discount + separate commission accounting.

I've attached a breakdown with sensitivity to ACV and term length. If the customer is only committing 6 months, we need to reduce reseller commission to 12% or request a one-time onboarding fee from CloudResell.

[Attachment: margin_breakdown_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

-Marissa

Subject: Proposed structure & operational notes for Acme private offer

Hi Amy / team — thanks for the patience, looping in Partner Ops + Marketplace. Based on the model and finance guidance, here's the recommended structure we can operationalize quickly on AWS: 

1) Pricing mechanics (preferred):
   - Redwood list price per SKU remains the source of truth.
   - AWS private offer applied to customer: 12% off list (applies to the customer invoice).
   - Reseller commission: 18% revenue share to CloudResell, paid net-30 monthly by Redwood.

2) Why this approach: preserves token-level traceability, keeps customer discount visible in the marketplace UI, and lets us audit usage against payout.

3) SKU bundling note: we will not create a bundled SKU for this deal to avoid conflating customer pricing with partner margin. If the reseller needs a combined invoice, CloudResell can issue their own invoice for services/implementation.

4) Operational steps & timeline:
   - Redwood sends private offer draft (Marketplace console) — 1 business day to prepare.
   - Acme confirms PO and accepts private offer — typically 2–3 business days.
   - CloudResell registers for payout & partner designation (if not already) — 3–5 business days.

5) Next actions: Priyom — can you confirm final ACV & contract term? Amy — once we have PO amount & term we'll send the private offer link.

Attachments: private_offer_playbook.pdf (private-offer flow + DocuSign template)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Operations
Redwood Inference
